courses.title: Construction Cost Estimating and Cost Control
The Construction Industry: The Way Forward

modules.title: Course Overview
modules.summary: Introduction to the specialization and to this course, glossary, and course policies. Light week-one material.

modules.title: Construction Industry Overview
modules.summary: Industry experts introduce the engineering and construction industry, compare program management, project management, and construction management, contrast construction with manufacturing, and walk through the Engineering-Architecture-Construction (EAC) lifecycle and the cost of change over it.

days.coursework: Module 1: course intro videos, glossary, pre-course survey
days.practical: Pick the one active company job to use all semester. Write a one-page summary of its scope: what is being built, where, for whom, rough budget and schedule.

days.coursework: Module 2, first half: industry intro, PgM vs PM vs CM, self-check quizzes
days.practical: List every party on the job (owner, architect, engineers, lender, GC, subs, city) and what each does. Note whether the company is acting as GC, CM, or developer on it.

days.coursework: Module 2, second half: construction vs manufacturing, EAC lifecycle, cost of change, module quiz
days.practical: Place the job on the EAC lifecycle (design, procurement, construction, closeout). Find one change that happened after design was done and ask the PM what it cost.

modules.title: Project Delivery
modules.summary: The project development cycle, contract types (lump sum, cost-plus, GMP), delivery methods (design-bid-build, design-build, CM at risk, CM as agency, alliance contracting, public-private partnerships), and the basics of surety bonding.

modules.title: Lean Project Delivery
modules.summary: An architect explains lean project delivery and lean design behaviors: stripping unnecessary effort, time, and cost out of planning, design, and construction to deliver what the owner values.

days.coursework: Module 3, first half: project development cycle, contract types, delivery methods, contracting strategy
days.practical: Read the job's prime contract. Identify the contract type and delivery method. Write down why the owner chose them, then check the answer with the PM.

days.coursework: Module 3, second half: CM at risk vs agency, alliance contracting and P3, surety bonds, module quiz
days.practical: Find out whether the job is bonded and what the surety required. List 3 risks the contract shifts onto the contractor.

days.coursework: Module 4: lean theory, lean design and delivery, flow, lean quiz
days.practical: Walk the site or sit in a sub meeting looking only for waste: waiting, rework, double handling, excess motion. Write down 3 examples and one fix for each.

modules.title: Sustainability in the Construction Industry
modules.summary: Skanska's sustainability director on sustainable development, safety, community involvement, and rating systems, focusing on the Envision rating system.

modules.title: Environment, Health and Safety of Construction Processes
modules.summary: Skanska's chief environmental officer on EHS practices, barriers to learning and change, safety performance models, and management systems.

modules.title: Building Information Modeling and Technology Trends in Construction
modules.summary: What BIM is, how it is used across the project lifecycle by the construction manager, design manager, and facility manager, and virtual reality in construction management.

days.coursework: Module 5: sustainability, safety, community involvement, rating systems, module quiz
days.practical: List every sustainability or energy-code item on the job (insulation, windows, mechanical efficiency, stormwater, Chicago requirements). Ask the mentor whether any rating system was considered and why or why not.

days.coursework: Module 6: EHS practices, barriers to change, safety performance models, management systems, EHS quiz
days.practical: Walk the site with the super. Read the site safety plan or last toolbox talk. Note 3 hazards and the control in place for each.

days.coursework: Module 7, first part: defining BIM, the role of CM and design management, technology and the CM
days.practical: Open the job's drawing set or model. Find one coordination issue between trades (mechanical vs structure, plumbing vs framing) and ask how it was caught and fixed.

modules.title: Building Information Modeling and Technology Trends in Construction
modules.summary: Facility management and virtual reality uses of BIM, technology quiz.

modules.title: International View of Construction Projects
modules.summary: Risk on international development projects: identifying types of risk, cost risks in construction and operations, and the ESPRIT framework for understanding risk.

modules.title: Role of a Construction Manager
modules.summary: What makes an effective project manager, building a project organizational chart, methods of contracting, potential project risks, logistics and planning, bidding and leveling sheets, change order and claim management. This is the most hands-on module in the course.

modules.title: Introduction to Project Planning
modules.summary: Project planning and scheduling, the work breakdown structure (WBS), standard and project coding, estimating activity durations, job logic, and activity relationships.

days.coursework: Module 7, finish: facility management, VR, technology quiz. Module 8: international development and project risk
days.practical: Inventory every piece of software and technology the company uses on the job (drawings, scheduling, accounting, field reporting, BIM). Interview one team member about what works and what does not.

days.coursework: Module 8, finish: cost risks, ESPRIT framework, quiz. Module 9, first part: effective PM, project org chart, methods of contracting
days.practical: Draw the job's project org chart: owner side, design side, contractor side, with names and roles. Mark who signs off on what.

days.coursework: Module 9, finish: project risks, logistics, bidding and leveling, change orders, quiz. Module 10, start: planning and scheduling intro
days.practical: Start a risk register for the job: 5 risks across cost, schedule, and safety, with likelihood, impact, and who owns each. Pull 2 past change orders and trace each from cause to approval.

modules.title: Introduction to Project Planning
modules.summary: The bulk of the course's hands-on work: building a WBS, coding it, estimating durations, determining job logic, and drawing activity relationships. Two 90-minute peer-reviewed exercises (WBS and job logic diagram) plus a duration work problem and a module quiz.

days.coursework: Module 10: planning process, WBS, standard and project coding, WBS exercise
days.practical: Build a 3-level WBS for the job in Excel using the company's cost codes.

days.coursework: Module 10: estimating activity duration 1–2, job logic, activity relationships, duration work problem
days.practical: Pick 10 activities from the WBS and estimate durations with crew size and productivity. Compare with the super's numbers and note the gaps.

days.coursework: Module 10: job logic diagram exercise, module quiz, post-course survey. **Course 1 complete.**
days.practical: Draw the job logic (which of the 10 activities depends on which). **Checkpoint:** present the scope summary, org chart, risk register, WBS, and logic diagram to the mentor.

modules.title: Introduction to Construction Scheduling
modules.summary: Course overview: activity relationships, scheduling procedures, critical path, calendar vs work dates, and uncertainty.

modules.title: Bar
modules.summary: Gantt charts as a scheduling tool, their uses, advantages, and disadvantages.

modules.title: Activity Precedence Diagrams
modules.summary: Activity-on-node (AON) diagrams that graphically represent activities and their relationships, with recommendations and worked examples.

modules.title: Types of Construction Activity Relationships
modules.summary: Finish-to-start, start-to-start, finish-to-finish, and multiple relationships, and how to show them on a precedence diagram.

modules.title: Forward and Backward Pass Calculations
modules.summary: Computing earliest and latest dates for every activity and the minimum project duration, with two worked examples and a one-hour quiz.

days.coursework: Modules 1–2: course intro, glossary, Gantt charts, Gantt quiz
days.practical: Get the job's current schedule from the PM. Read it as a Gantt chart and write 5 questions about it. Find out who maintains it and how often.

days.coursework: Modules 3–4: AON diagrams, activity relationships, relationships quiz
days.practical: Convert the 10 activities from week 5 into an AON diagram. Mark which relationships the real schedule uses (most will be finish-to-start; find at least one that is not).

days.coursework: Module 5: forward and backward pass, examples, quiz
days.practical: Run the forward and backward pass by hand on the 10-activity diagram. Write early start, early finish, late start, late finish on every node.

modules.title: Critical Path
modules.summary: What the critical path is, why it matters, how many there can be, lags, and critical path under start-to-start and finish-to-finish relationships.

modules.title: Activity Floats
modules.summary: Total float, free float, interfering float, and independent float.

modules.title: Understanding Work Dates and Calendar Dates
modules.summary: Working days vs calendar days and charting both in a project plan.

modules.title: Activity on Arrow
modules.summary: Drawing activity-on-arrow diagrams, numbering nodes, advanced diagrams, backward pass, and determining project duration; two assignments.

days.coursework: Module 6: critical path, lags, SS and FF cases, CPM quiz
days.practical: Identify the critical path on the real job schedule. Confirm with the PM or scheduler whether they agree, and why the schedule shows what it shows.

days.coursework: Modules 7–8: floats, work vs calendar dates, floats and calendar quiz
days.practical: Compute total and free float for 5 non-critical activities. Convert 3 activities from work days to calendar dates using the company's calendar (holidays, weather days).

days.coursework: Module 9: activity on arrow videos and first quiz
days.practical: Redraw the 10-activity network as an activity-on-arrow diagram. Check that the project duration matches the AON answer.

modules.title: Activity on Arrow
modules.summary: Activity diagram and critical path assignment.

modules.title: PERT and Range Estimating
modules.summary: Program Evaluation and Review Technique for uncertain durations: probability of finishing in a given number of days, worked examples, and range estimating.

modules.title: The Role of the Scheduler in Construction Management
modules.summary: An STV scheduler on keeping a project on track and keeping accurate progress records.

modules.title: Linear Construction Operations and Line of Balance
modules.summary: Scheduling repetitive work (floors, units, roadway) with the line-of-balance method.

days.coursework: Module 9, finish: activity diagram and critical path assignment. Module 10: PERT videos
days.practical: For 5 critical activities, ask the super for optimistic, most likely, and pessimistic durations. Compute the PERT expected duration for each.

days.coursework: Module 10, finish: discussion. Module 11: role of the scheduler, PERT and scheduler quiz
days.practical: Compute the probability the job finishes by the contract date using the PERT numbers. Sit in on the weekly schedule or sub coordination meeting and note how progress is recorded.

days.coursework: Module 12: linear construction, line of balance, LOB quiz and diagram
days.practical: Pick a repetitive scope on the job (units, floors, rooms). Draw a line-of-balance for 2 trades across the units and find where one crew waits on the other.

modules.title: Technology Applications for Scheduling
modules.summary: Overviews of MS Project and Primavera P6 (critical path, Gantt, importing activities), schedule analysis tools, custom tools, BIM scheduling tools, and integrating model and schedule.

modules.title: Scheduling for Large Programs
modules.summary: The integrated master schedule for multi-project programs.

modules.title: Risk Allocation and Planning
modules.summary: AECOM's deputy director of risk management on formal risk management, risk profiles, risk assessment, and using risk as a planning and scheduling tool.

days.coursework: Module 13, first part: software overview, MS Project, Primavera P6
days.practical: Rebuild the 10-activity schedule in whatever tool the company uses (MS Project, P6, Procore, or Excel). Compare its critical path with the hand calculation.

days.coursework: Module 13, finish: schedule analysis, custom tools, BIM tools, technology quiz. Module 14: large programs
days.practical: Update the real schedule against actual progress. Note what slipped and why. Write a 3-week look-ahead.

days.coursework: Module 15: risk allocation and planning
days.practical: Build a schedule risk register: 5 schedule risks with likelihood and impact, which activities they hit, and how much contingency each deserves.

modules.title: Lean Design in Construction Scheduling
modules.summary: Lean time and schedule, flow, lean design and lean scheduling, plus the final quiz on large programs, risk, and lean.

modules.title: Cost Estimating and Cost Control Overview
modules.summary: Course introduction and glossary.

modules.title: Understanding Design in the Construction Industry
modules.summary: A Turner and Townsend project manager on the stages of design in a construction project.

modules.title: Introduction to the Types of Cost Estimates
modules.summary: Types of estimates, cost indices, and the cost-capacity factor, with a work problem.

days.coursework: Module 16: lean scheduling, final quiz, post-course survey. **Course 2 complete.**
days.practical: **Checkpoint:** present the updated schedule, look-ahead, line-of-balance, and schedule risk register to the mentor. Flag one recovery idea for a delayed task.

days.coursework: Course 3, Modules 1–2: course intro, glossary, stages of design, design quiz
days.practical: Pull the job's drawing set. Identify the design stage of each package (schematic, design development, construction documents) and ask the architect or PM what is still outstanding.

days.coursework: Module 3: types of estimates, cost indices, cost-capacity factor, quiz and work problem
days.practical: Find the job's original conceptual estimate and the current budget. Compute how far they moved. Apply a cost index to a past company deal to restate it in 2027 dollars.

modules.title: Quantity Take-Off and Measurement
modules.summary: Turner and Townsend cost managers on takeoff: cut and fill, deep and concrete foundations, formwork, concrete takeoff examples, rebar, structural steel, masonry, curtain wall, facade and wall finishes.

modules.title: Pricing
modules.summary: Material costs, formwork, reinforcing and concrete, the money and productivity components of labor cost, and estimating equipment costs.

days.coursework: Module 4, first part: measurement, cut and fill, deep foundations, concrete foundations and formwork
days.practical: Do a concrete takeoff for one element on the job (footings, a slab, or a wall) from the drawings: volume, formwork area, rebar weight.

days.coursework: Module 4, finish: concrete and steel takeoff examples, rebar, structural steel, takeoff quiz
days.practical: Do a second takeoff for a finish trade (drywall, masonry, or flooring) for one unit or area.

days.coursework: Module 5: materials, formwork, labor money and productivity, equipment, pricing quiz
days.practical: Price both takeoffs with real unit costs from a recent sub bid or the company's cost history. Split each into labor, material, and equipment.

modules.title: Building the Estimate
modules.summary: Estimate classification, methods and formats, a schematic design estimate demo, finalizing, and due diligence checks.

modules.title: Procurement
modules.summary: Pre-bid estimate, bid documentation, bid stage, bid returns, and bid leveling.

modules.title: Post Contract and Cost Estimation within a Project
modules.summary: Cost reporting, change orders, and communication.

modules.title: Construction Cost Control Methods
modules.summary: What cost control is and the methods used.

modules.title: Earned Value Method
modules.summary: EVM parameters, performance examples, favorable and unfavorable performance, calculating EVM, with a work problem.

days.coursework: Modules 6–7: building the estimate, procurement, both quizzes
days.practical: Assemble the two takeoffs into a mini estimate with overhead and markup. Gather the sub bids for one trade on the job and build a bid leveling sheet.

days.coursework: Modules 8–9: cost reporting, change orders, cost control methods, both quizzes
days.practical: Pick one budget line on the job. Match every invoice and commitment to it and report committed vs spent vs remaining.

days.coursework: Module 10: earned value method, EVM quiz and work problem
days.practical: Compute planned value, earned value, actual cost, CPI, and SPI for the job (or one trade) from the latest pay application and schedule update.

modules.title: Close Out Period
modules.summary: Punch list review and close-out activities.

modules.title: Cost Estimation in Practice
modules.summary: Tips in estimating and cost management, and roles and responsibilities of cost managers.

modules.title: Project Cash Flow
modules.summary: A Gilbane PM on cash vs accrual, contractor cash flow, billing, the payment cycle and its delays, schedule of values, front loading, and delaying expenses.

modules.title: Technology Trends in Cost Estimating and Cost Control
modules.summary: 5D estimating with BIM, estimating software, workflows, and implementation.

days.coursework: Modules 11–12: close out, estimating in practice, both quizzes
days.practical: Review the punch list and close-out package from a recently finished company job. List what the owner and lender required before final payment.

days.coursework: Module 13, first part: cash flow and accrual, contractor cash flow, billing, payment cycle
days.practical: Follow one pay application on the job end to end: schedule of values, percent complete, retainage, lien waivers, and when the money actually arrived.

days.coursework: Module 13, finish: schedule of values, front loading, delaying expenses, cash flow quiz. Module 14: technology trends
days.practical: Chart the job's cash flow month by month in Excel (billings in, costs out). Find the peak negative cash position and how the company funds it.

modules.title: Program Cost Estimating
modules.summary: Cost control for large capital programs.

modules.title: Lean in Cost Control
modules.summary: Benchmarking and normalization, lean value, lean in cost control, and set-based design, plus the final quiz.

modules.title: Introduction to the Construction Finance Course
modules.summary: Course overview, formula sheet, glossary.

modules.title: The Mathematics of Money
modules.summary: Time value of money, simple and compound interest, nominal vs effective rates, minimum attractive rate of return, present and future value, uniform series, net present value, and internal rate of return, with a case study.

days.coursework: Modules 15–16: program cost control, lean in cost control, final quiz, post-course survey. **Course 3 complete.**
days.practical: **Checkpoint:** present a cost report for the job to the mentor: budget vs committed vs spent vs projected over/under, with the EVM indices and cash-flow chart.

days.coursework: Course 4, Module 1: intro, formula sheet, glossary. Module 2, first part: time value of money, simple and compound interest, nominal and effective rates
days.practical: Read the job's construction loan term sheet. List rate, index, spread, loan-to-cost, reserves, term, and extension options. Compute the effective annual rate.

days.coursework: Module 2, second part: present and future value, uniform series
days.practical: Compute one month of interest carry on the construction loan at the current drawn balance. Then project carry for the rest of the job from the draw schedule.

modules.title: The Mathematics of Money
modules.summary: NPV and IRR examples, Mathematics of Money quiz and case study.

modules.title: Real Estate Finance for Development Projects
modules.summary: Columbia's Anthony Webster on the real estate project lifecycle, zoning code parameters, development costs, estimating sale price by comps and by cap rate, discounted cash flow, NPV and IRR for project evaluation, NPV and IRR in Excel, and compounding periods. The module closest to the developer's job.

days.coursework: Module 2, finish: NPV and IRR examples, quiz, case study
days.practical: Build NPV and IRR in Excel for a past company deal using its actual cash flows. Check the IRR against what the mentor remembers the deal returning.

days.coursework: Module 3, first part: financing development projects, feasibility study parameters, development costs, comps-based and cap-rate-based sale
days.practical: Pull the Chicago zoning for the job's parcel: district, FAR, height, setbacks, parking. Compute the maximum buildable area and compare with what was built.

days.coursework: Module 3, finish: DCF framework, NPV and IRR methods, NPV and IRR in Excel, compounding periods, both assignments
days.practical: Estimate the finished project's value two ways: comparable sales and cap rate on projected NOI. Compare with the lender's appraisal.

modules.title: Financial Plans for Development Projects
modules.summary: Debt financing, a construction loan example, net cash flows for sponsor and lender, DCF evaluation from both sides, and decision tree analysis with and without time value.

modules.title: Project Finance
modules.summary: Global project finance by sector, stakeholders and their roles, principles of project financing, risk allocation, sponsor and government perspectives, contract parties and agreements.

days.coursework: Module 4, first part: financial plans, debt financing, construction loan example, sponsor and lender cash flows, DCF for both
days.practical: Rebuild the job's sources and uses in Excel. Draw the capital stack (senior debt, any mezzanine, sponsor equity) with amounts and percentages.

days.coursework: Module 4, finish: decision tree analysis 1–2, example in Excel, results with time value, module quiz
days.practical: Build a two-branch decision tree for a real choice on the job (two finish levels, build now vs wait, lease vs sell). Solve it in Excel with the mentor's probabilities.

days.coursework: Module 5: project finance overview, stakeholders, risk allocation, sponsor and government perspectives, contracts, quiz
days.practical: Map the job's stakeholders and who bears each risk: cost overrun, delay, lease-up, interest rate, completion. Ask the mentor 5 questions about how the lender protects itself.

modules.title: Risk in Project Finance
modules.summary: Project parties and timeline, borrowing vs partnering, and a developer land-swap case.

modules.title: Public-Private Partnerships
modules.summary: P3 concept, project types, structures, risk transfer, success factors, benefits, and case studies.

modules.title: Lean in Construction Financing
modules.summary: Identifying and mitigating risk through lean project delivery.

modules.title: Introduction
modules.summary: History and development of the construction industry, common industry characteristics, and internal challenges, including a reading on the impact of COVID-19. Most of the 3 hours is readings and discussion prompts.

days.coursework: Modules 6–7: risk in project finance, public-private partnerships, both quizzes
days.practical: Follow one draw request end to end: pay app, lien waivers, inspector's report, title update, lender funding. Assemble a mock draw package for next month.

days.coursework: Modules 8–9: lean in financing, quiz, wrap-up, post-course survey. **Course 4 complete.**
days.practical: **Checkpoint:** present the sources and uses, capital stack, interest carry projection, NPV/IRR model, and mock draw package to the mentor.

days.coursework: Course 5, Module 1: history, characteristics, internal challenges, module quiz (skim the policy readings)
days.practical: Write one page on where time is lost on the job: the company's own productivity challenges, with examples from the semester.

modules.title: Trends in the Construction Industry
modules.summary: Ten trends reshaping construction: aging infrastructure, the investment gap, climate change, sustainability, urbanization, workforce shortage, and complex regulation.

modules.title: Transformations Needed: Industry and Government Level
modules.summary: Industry transformation on marketing, and government transformation on regulations, policies, and procurement.

modules.title: Transformations Needed: Companies Level
modules.summary: Company transformation on strategy, workforce and culture, and process and operations.

modules.title: New and Rising Innovative Technologies
modules.summary: Big data, AI and machine learning, 3D printing, drones and robotics, VR and AR, digital twins, and the four industrial revolutions.

days.coursework: Module 2: ten trends, trends quiz
days.practical: Pick the 3 trends that hit the company's Chicago work hardest. Write a paragraph on each: what it changes for the company and one response.

days.coursework: Modules 3–4: industry, government, and company transformations, both quizzes
days.practical: Interview the mentor on the company's strategy, workforce, and processes. Identify one process improvement the company could make this year.

days.coursework: Module 5: new technologies, quiz, post-course survey. **Course 5 and specialization complete.**
days.practical: **Final presentation** to the mentor: the full semester package for the job (schedule, cost tracking, finance model, draw package) plus the one improvement for the company.

checkpoints.title: Construction Project Management
checkpoints.presents: Scope summary, org chart, risk register, WBS, job logic diagram

checkpoints.title: Construction Scheduling
checkpoints.presents: Updated CPM schedule, 3-week look-ahead, line-of-balance, schedule risk register

checkpoints.title: Cost Estimating and Cost Control
checkpoints.presents: Cost report with EVM indices and cash-flow chart; takeoffs, mini estimate, bid leveling

checkpoints.title: Construction Finance
checkpoints.presents: Sources and uses, capital stack, interest carry, NPV/IRR, mock draw package

checkpoints.title: The Way Forward
checkpoints.presents: Final presentation of the whole package plus one improvement for the company
